data.body: Fixes bug B-suite-lock-held-by-n1-run: the load-based worker clamp gave the lock holder 1 worker; the holder should get a floor of workers (ci.suite_min_workers) so it does not hog the host-wide lock. Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-suite-lock-held-by-n1-run --regression-test <test>`.
data.title: Fix bug B-suite-lock-held-by-n1-run: suite lock held for hours by a full suite at pytest -n 1

data.text: Fix B-suite-lock-held-by-n1-run and the listed ci-infra bugs one at a time, each fully gated and merged (lead brief to fx-ci-infra)

data.claim: workers.compute clamps floor(cores*0.75-loadavg) to min_workers=1 even for the lock holder, so a loaded host yields -n 1
data.falsifier: compute with load*cores > cores*high returns >1 for a holder
data.mechanism: ci._execute calls _with_workers/localize_hooks after SL.hold with no holder floor
data.probe: pytest tests/test_auto_workers.py -k holder on unfixed code
data.probe_output: TypeError: compute() got an unexpected keyword holding_suite (4 failed on unfixed)
data.question: Why did the suite-lock holder run at -n 1?

evidence.note: research note CONFIRMED: holder gets -n 1 under load; regression tests fail on unfixed code
reviewed r-small-files/r-everything-configurable: new knob ci.suite_min_workers with upgrade note; files <20KB; no hardcoded tunables
commit 539d3b731; tests/test_auto_workers.py + architecture guards pass (63)

chunk_findings.detail: `holding_suite` is derived from `local`, but `local` is true for any locally executed run, not only for the full-suite lock holder. A local selected-test run (`scope.scope == "selected"` and `local=True`) on a loaded host can have its worker clamp computed as 1 worker, yet `_with_workers(..., holding_suite=local)` and `localize_hooks(..., holding_suite=True)` raise it to `ci.suite_min_workers` (default 8). That bypasses the load clamp even though the selected run does not hold the host-wide full-suite lock described by the fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:553-557

chunk_findings.detail: The new `holding_suite` flag is wired to the pre-existing `local` argument: `_with_workers(cmd, cfg, used, "command", holding_suite=local)` and `localize_hooks(..., holding_suite=True)` under `if local`. `local` controls whether pre-commit localisation happens, not whether this run holds the host-wide full-suite lock. Given `_prepare(local=True)` for a `scope` where `scope.scope == "selected"` (a selected run that holds no suite lock), the command is resolved with the holder floor and can overcommit the host; given a full-suite lock holder invoked with `local=False`, the command can still be clamped to `-n 1`, leaving B-suite-lock-held-by-n1-run unfixed on that path. The condition should be an explicit lock-holder flag, not `local`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_prepare

chunk_findings.detail: `_under_memory_pressure` floors the high-memory halving at `lo`, not at the suite-holder floor `held`. Given a suite-lock holder with `min_workers=1`, `max_workers=16`, `suite_min_workers=8`, `workers="auto"`, and a high load that the load clamp would otherwise reduce below 8, `compute` first produces `n=8` via the new floor. If memory pressure is high but not critical (for example `free=0.10`, so `pressure=0.90` with the default high mark `0.85`), this line returns `max(1, 8 // 2) = 4`, silently dropping the holder below `suite_min_workers`. That can recreate the original suite-lock-hogging condition; only the critical-memory case is covered by the new test, so this high-memory bypass is uncaught.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workers.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest shows the actual full-suite pytest command path was also changed in `ddflow/services/ci.py` via `_with_workers`, but none of the added tests import or execute that path; every new test calls `WK.compute` or `WK.localize_auto` directly with `holding_suite=True`. If `_with_workers` forgets to propagate `holding_suite=True` into `WK.compute`/`WK.localize_auto`, a busy host still gives the lock holder `-n 1`, while all added unit tests pass. The regression coverage therefore does not exercise the changed integration point most likely to reintroduce the original bug.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_auto_workers.py:test_suite_lock_holder_is_not_clamped_to_one_worker (missing integration coverage)

chunk_findings.detail: The test passes both a list-style placeholder, `args: [-n, auto]`, and a string-style placeholder, `x: -n auto`, but only asserts `"-n 8" in text`. A buggy `localize_auto` that replaces only `x: -n auto` and leaves the actual `args: [-n, auto]` unchanged still makes this assertion pass, so the test does not verify the list form provided as input is actually localized to `-n 8`.

data.body:
Fixes bug Bfdcb5c177c: A review run killed before its verdict (shell/tool exit) is still charged a round: fix-B-suite-lock... rubber_duck showed 2/4 after one finished review plus one killed mid-flight. An interrupted review that recorded nothing should not consume the budget.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bfdcb5c177c --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bfdcb5c177c --regression-test <test>` first).

chunk_findings.detail: The rename from `_execute(..., local=...)` to `_execute(..., holding_suite=...)` was applied to the definition and to the full-suite call at `ddflow/services/ci.py:422`, but the selected-scope `_prepare` path cited in previous finding 1 is unchanged: it still calls `_execute(..., local=True)` for a run where `scope.scope == "selected"`. Because `_execute` no longer accepts a `local` keyword, that call now raises `TypeError: _execute() got an unexpected keyword argument 'local'` before any selected run can execute. This is not just the original semantic overcommit issue; the selected path is now broken entirely.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_prepare

chunk_findings.detail: In `_under_memory_pressure`, the high-memory branch returns `max(held, n // 2)`. For `compute`’s explicit `workers` setting, `n` is not first floored to `held`; the new `held` clamp was only added to the `else`/`auto` branch. Given `cfg.ci.workers="2"`, `min_workers=1`, `max_workers=16`, `suite_min_workers=8`, `holding_suite=True`, `files=10`, and `free=0.10` (`pressure=0.90`, above the default high mark `0.85`), the explicit branch yields `n=2`, then this line returns `max(8, 2 // 2) == 8`. A healthy host returns 2, and a memory-pressured host returns 8, so memory pressure is increasing the worker count; if `suite_min_workers` is intended as a holder floor for explicit settings, the normal-memory explicit path is equally wrong because it never floors to 8.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workers.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The revised probe does not answer prior finding 4: the list-style placeholder `args: [-n, auto]` has been removed, leaving only string-style `-n auto` lines and an exact text assertion. A `localize_auto` implementation that still fails to rewrite list-style placeholders would produce the exact expected text and pass, so the list-style path remains unverified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_auto_workers.py:test_localize_auto_gives_the_holder_its_floor

chunk_findings.detail: With `holding_suite=True` and an explicit `ci.workers` smaller than `ci.suite_min_workers`, high memory pressure now raises the worker count instead of halving it. Example: `min_workers=1`, `max_workers=16`, `workers=4`, `suite_min_workers=8`, and a signal source reporting `free=0.10`, so `pressure=0.90 > warn=0.85`. The unchanged `setting != "auto"` branch sets `n=4`; `_under_memory_pressure` then returns `max(held=8, 4 // 2) = 8`. `compute` now reports 8 workers with `inputs["memory"]="high: halved"`, while the same call with no memory pressure reports 4. Memory pressure must not increase the worker count; this would make a suite-lock holder spawn twice its explicit workers exactly when the host is already under memory pressure.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workers.py:_under_memory_pressure

chunk_findings.detail: The `holding_suite=False` branch asserts only `not any(flags)`, but `not any([])` is true, so the assertion passes even if `_execute` never calls `WK.compute` for non-holders. A broken `_execute` that leaves non-holder commands/hooks with `-n auto` or `-n {workers}` unchanged would still pass this test, because `Fake.run` returns `code=0` and `flags` stays `[]`. The assertion should be `assert flags and not any(flags)` to prove the non-holder path actually consulted the worker computation and passed `False`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_parity_workers.py:test_execute_gives_only_the_lock_holder_the_worker_floor

chunk_findings.detail: The previous explicit-count/floor interaction is still present. With `ci.workers="2"`, `ci.min_workers=1`, `ci.max_workers=16`, `ci.suite_min_workers=8`, `holding_suite=True`, `files=10`, and `free=0.10`, `compute` enters the explicit branch with `n=2`. `_under_memory_pressure` computes `pressure=0.90 > 0.85` and returns `max(held, n // 2) = max(8, 1) = 8`. That raises an explicit worker count above the user's setting, and does so under memory pressure rather than halving it. The cited `test_an_explicit_worker_count_is_never_raised_by_the_holder_floor` does not answer this scenario unless it also forces the same high-memory input; the code path itself is still wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workers.py:_under_memory_pressure

chunk_findings.detail: `localize_auto` still only uses `_AUTO = r"(?<![\w-])-n\s+auto(?![\w-])"`, which requires whitespace immediately after `-n`. A valid pre-commit list placeholder such as `args: [-n, auto]`, which has a comma after `-n`, does not match. For `text = "  args: [-n, auto]\n"`, the function returns `(text, None)` unchanged, leaving `auto` in the localized pre-commit config. The cited `test_localize_auto_gives_the_holder_its_floor` probe does not exercise this list-style path, so the earlier gap remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workers.py:localize_auto

chunk_findings.detail: The newly added test only feeds `WK.localize_auto` the string-style placeholder text `"x: -n auto\ny: -n auto\n"`. It never exercises the list-style placeholder form, e.g. `args: [-n, auto]`, that the prior findings flagged. A broken `localize_auto` implementation which rewrites string-style `-n auto` but still fails to rewrite list-style placeholders would return the exact asserted text and `w.n == 8`, so this probe passes while the list-style path remains unverified. The cited triage probe is this same test and contains no list-style placeholder, so it does not answer the finding.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_auto_workers.py:test_localize_auto_gives_the_holder_its_floor

chunk_findings.detail: The test records every `WK.compute` call into one unlabeled `flags` list, so it cannot prove the main command path called `compute` at all. The setup writes `CI.PRE_COMMIT_CONFIG` with `HOOK`, meaning hook localization alone can populate `flags`. A broken `_execute` that never calls `WK.compute` for the main `"pytest -n {workers} tests/test_a.py"` command would still leave `flags=[True]` for `holding_suite=True` and `flags=[False]` for `holding_suite=False`; both pass the assertions because they only check that no flag is wrong, not that a command-level call occurred. The docstring claims the flag is verified “for both the command and the localized hooks,” but the assertion does not enforce the command half.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_parity_workers.py:test_execute_gives_only_the_lock_holder_the_worker_floor

chunk_findings.detail: The `head` callback runs `G.run(tree, "show", f"HEAD:{path}", binary=True, timeout=P.TIMEOUTS["git_listing"])`, but `tree` is the result of `_index_tree(repo)`—a Git tree id/index object, not a repository working directory. `G.run` expects the repo path as its first positional argument, so whenever `complexity_warn_at > 0` and at least one path is staged, this either raises `FileNotFoundError` and aborts the commit despite the advisory-only guarantee, or `r.ok` is false and `head` returns `None` for every existing function, making `CB.risen` compute the advisory against the wrong baseline.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:1388 `_complexity_note`

chunk_findings.detail: The module-level `pytest.importorskip("radon")` skips the whole file whenever `radon` is absent, so `test_without_radon_nothing_is_claimed` never executes in the exact environment it is meant to validate. Given the commit’s stated requirement “silent without radon”, a no-radon CI run would see this test SKIPPED and could pass even if `ddflow.services.complexity_budget` now raises an `ImportError` on the no-radon path. The no-radon test should run when radon is missing (with only the radon-dependent tests skipped), or there should be an explicit no-radon import check.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_commit_complexity_budget.py:16

chunk_findings.detail: The verdict string unconditionally says `grade D: tests/test_architecture_guards.py will fail` whenever a touched function has `cc >= GRADE_D_FROM` and increased from HEAD. That guard fails only when a module's count of functions above 20 rises. Given a function already at CC 21 in HEAD that is changed to CC 22, `risen()` emits "... will fail" even though the module's count above 20 is unchanged and the guard will not fail. This makes the advisory state a false CI failure for any already-grade-D function that simply becomes more complex.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/complexity_budget.py:58

chunk_findings.detail: The inner `head` does `G.run(tree, "show", f"HEAD:{path}", ...)`, but `tree` is the value returned by `_index_tree(repo)` — the existing helper whose result is used as the index-tree id in `staged_bytes(repo, p, tree=tree)`. That is not a working-directory path. For any staged file already present in HEAD, `git show HEAD:<path>` must be run with `repo` as the cwd/repository argument, not with the index-tree id. With a staged edit to an existing file containing an unchanged function whose CC is already 20, `head` fails (or `G.run` receives a nonexistent cwd), so `CB.risen` has no HEAD baseline and either reports the unchanged function as newly risen or fails to report a real rise. The call should pass `repo`, not `tree`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:_complexity_note

chunk_findings.detail: `pytest.importorskip("radon")` is at module scope, so when radon is not installed—the exact environment in which the “silent without radon” fallback must work—the whole test module is skipped and `test_without_radon_nothing_is_claimed` never runs. The test instead only simulates the absence by monkeypatching `CB.cc_visit = None` after radon has already been successfully imported, which is not the real missing-dependency path. A regression where `CB.complexities` or `E.check_commit` crashes on actual missing radon would not fail CI.

chunk_findings.detail: `complexities()` filters out every block with a `methods` attribute, but radon’s `cc_visit` represents a class as the block whose `methods` list holds its method `Function` objects; those methods are not also separate top-level blocks. The comment on line 36 is wrong. Given a staged `.py` file whose method `C.m` rises from CC 17 to 18 (above the default `complexity_warn_at`), the only returned block is `Class C` (which has `methods`), so `complexities(staged(path))` returns `{}`, `risen()` emits nothing, and `advice()` returns `""`; the commit hook misses the method entirely. This is the previous class-method finding and still holds: the code has not been changed to traverse `b.methods` or inner classes.

chunk_findings.detail: The `head` callback still runs `G.run(tree, "show", f"HEAD:{path}", ...)`, but `tree` is the result of `_index_tree(repo)`—a Git tree id/index object, not a repository working directory. `G.run` expects the repo path as its first positional argument, so with `complexity_warn_at > 0` and at least one staged path this attempts to `chdir` into a SHA string and raises `FileNotFoundError`, aborting an allowed commit despite the advisory-only guarantee (or otherwise never successfully reads `HEAD:<path>`). chunk_findings.detail: The line `verdict = f"grade D: {GUARD} will fail"` is emitted whenever a function crosses from below `GRADE_D_FROM` to `GRADE_D_FROM` or more, independent of the module-level count the architecture guard actually monitors. A concrete counterexample: HEAD `mod.py` has `def a()` at CC 22 and `def b()` at CC 20; staged refactors `a` down to CC 20 and adds one `if` to `b`, raising it to CC 21. The module’s count of functions above 20 remains 1, so `tests/test_architecture_guards.py` will not fail, but `risen` reports `b` as `"grade D: tests/test_architecture_guards.py will fail"`. This is a new false CI-failure claim, distinct from the already-grade-D case fixed in this round.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/complexity_budget.py:risen

chunk_findings.detail: `head()` still passes `tree = _index_tree(repo)` as the first argument to `G.run`, but `_index_tree(repo)` is the pre-existing index-tree id used to read staged blobs via `staged_bytes(repo, p, tree=tree)`, not a filesystem path. With a staged edit to an existing file in HEAD, `G.run(tree, "show", f"HEAD:{path}", ...)` tries to use that hex id as the git working directory, so the `show` fails/does not return `r.ok` and `head` returns `None`; `CB.risen` then cannot see the function’s previous complexity and emits the wrong advisory (for example treating an already grade-D function as newly introduced rather than “already grade D, getting worse”). The cited test probe does not answer the defect unless it runs `_complexity_note` with the real `_index_tree(repo)` value as the cwd; a test that stubs `_index_tree` to a worktree Path will still pass. The `show HEAD:<path>` command should run with `repo` as the repository/cwd, or otherwise derive the repository path rather than reusing `tree`.

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 3 is only partially answered. chunk_findings.detail: `complexities()` collapses radon’s block list into a `dict` keyed by `b.fullname`. Radon emits the same `fullname` for multiple definitions of the same top-level function in one file (for example, two `def setup():` definitions under `if sys.platform == ...`). The dict keeps only the last block, so `risen()` can miss a complexity increase in an earlier definition. Input: HEAD has two `setup` definitions, both CC 1. Staged raises the first `setup` to CC 18 while leaving the second unchanged. `complexities(staged)` returns only the second block (`{'setup': (line_of_second, 1)}`), `before.get('setup')[1]` is also 1, so no warning is emitted even though the touched function crossed `complexity_warn_at`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/complexity_budget.py:37

chunk_findings.detail: `source.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")` ignores PEP 263 encoding declarations. A valid staged `.py` file declaring `# -*- coding: latin-1 -*-` and defining `def café(...)` has a non-UTF-8 byte `0xe9` in the identifier; the replacement decoder turns it into U+FFFD, `cc_visit` raises `SyntaxError`, and the `except (SyntaxError, ValueError)` makes `complexities()` return `{}`. Any function whose complexity rose to `warn_at` in such a valid Python file is silently skipped, contradicting the feature’s promise to name touched functions at commit time.

chunk_findings.detail: The new knob doc says complexity “grade D starts at 21, which tests/test_architecture_guards.py refuses.” That is contradicted by the change’s own intent: the fixed `advice()` wording says the guard COUNTS grade D, not that it refuses merely for reaching grade D. chunk_findings.detail: `complexities()` collapses all definitions sharing a `fullname` to the single highest complexity, and `risen()` then only compares that one maximum before and after. This misses a rise in a *different* definition with the same name. Concrete input: HEAD `mod.py` has `if cond: def f(...): ...` at CC 30 and `else: def f(...): ...` at CC 5. A staged edit leaves the first branch at CC 30 and turns the second branch into CC 25. `before` is `{"f": (line_if, 30)}`; `staged` is also `{"f": (line_if, 30)}` because the second branch is still not the maximum. At `risen` line 66, `cc >= warn_at and cc > was` is `30 >= 21 and 30 > 30`, false, so no line is emitted. This violates the function's own stated contract of reporting a function whose complexity rose to `warn_at` or more, and it misses the architecture guard count rising from one `f` above 20 to two `f`s above 20, exactly the CI failure this hook exists to warn about.

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test only rejects the exact substring `"counted by"`. The prior bug it is meant to guard against was a false refusal wording such as `"... which tests/test_architecture_guards.py refuses"` for a function already at grade D that gets worse; that wording does not contain `"counted by"`, so an `advice()` message like `m.py:1 near_limit CC 21 -> 22 (already grade D, getting worse), which tests/test_architecture_guards.py refuses` would still satisfy both of this test's assertions. Thus the test would pass under the exact previous erroneous message and does not actually guard against the refusal claim regressing.

data.summary: Only ci.py (_run_locked, SL.hold) takes the host-wide suite lock; the unit_tests gate (gates runner run_command_gate, command 'uv run pytest tests/ -n {workers}') and any hand-run pytest take none. So 'ddflow gate run X unit_tests' from several agents runs full suites concurrently (host load 236 with 3 suites and up to 177 xdist workers). Fix: hold SL.hold for a gate command that runs the whole suite (unit_tests default) in the gate runner, with the same queue/wait reason; manual runs cannot be locked, so the etiquette rule stays.

Fixes bug Bf37f016693: Only ci.py (_run_locked, SL.hold) takes the host-wide suite lock; the unit_tests gate (gates runner run_command_gate, command 'uv run pytest tests/ -n {workers}') and any hand-run pytest take none. So 'ddflow gate run X unit_tests' from several agents runs full suites concurrently (host load 236 with 3 suites and up to 177 xdist workers). Fix: hold SL.hold for a gate command that runs the whole suite (unit_tests default) in the gate runner, with the same queue/wait reason; manual runs cannot be locked, so the etiquette rule stays.

chunk_findings.detail: `complexities()` filters out every block with a `methods` attribute and relies on `cc_visit` itself to put class methods into the top-level block list, but `radon.complexity.cc_visit` returns class blocks at the top level and stores methods inside `Class.methods`; it does not list those method functions separately. So class methods are never analyzed. Given HEAD and staged both containing `class C:\n    def m(self, x): ...` with, say, CC 25, `complexities()` returns `{}` for both, and `risen()` emits no warning even though `m` is exactly the kind of function the check promises to name before the CI gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/complexity_budget.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: Duplicate definitions are disambiguated only by source order (`f`, `f#2`, ...), so deleting an earlier duplicate can make an unchanged later definition look like it “rose.” Concrete input: HEAD has two top-level `def f` definitions, the first CC 1 and the second CC 30. `before` is `{"f": (line1, 1), "f#2": (line2, 30)}`. Staged deletes the first definition and leaves the CC 30 one unchanged. `complexities(staged)` is then `{"f": (line2, 30)}`, and `risen()` compares it against `before["f"]` (CC 1), emitting `CC 1 -> 30` for a function whose complexity did not rise. This is a spurious commit-hook warning caused by the order-based matching.

chunk_findings.detail: The wait-evidence merge `_wait_evidence(gdef, p, out) or {"waited_s": lock_wait}` drops `lock_wait` whenever `_wait_evidence` is non-empty, even though that function already records the runner’s admission-slot wait (see `_waited`’s docstring). For a full-suite `unit_tests` gate that waits 8 s for the host suite lock and then waits 2 s for the `CommandRunner` admission slot, `_wait_evidence` returns `{"waited_s": 2.0}`, so the outer lock wait `8.0` is never reported. The two sources are sequential and additive, so the evidence under-reports total queueing time.
